title: Small-scale in situ Hi-C protocol for early embryos to resolve the three-dimensional genome structure
author: Song, Zhang, et al.

steps.title: End repair and A‑tailing
steps.instruction: Assemble the end‑repair/A‑tailing reaction on ice in a low‑binding tube using 17 µL fragmented double‑stranded DNA, 2.3 µL 10× End Repair & A‑Tailing Buffer, and 1 µL End Repair & A‑Tailing Enzyme Mix (total 20.3 µL). Vortex gently, spin down, then incubate in a thermocycler at 20 °C for 35 min, followed by 65 °C for 30 min (lid set to 85 °C). Hold at 4 °C briefly. Store the reaction at 23 °C for up to 24 h, at 4 °C for up to 3 days, or at –20 °C for up to 4 weeks. Cool to ≤20 °C before proceeding to adapter ligation.

steps.title: Adapter ligation
steps.instruction: Dilute adapter stock to 1 µM (1:14 dilution) in advance. On ice, pre‑mix 10 µL Ligase Buffer and 3 µL DNA Ligase, then add to the 20.3 µL A‑tailed DNA together with 1 µL 1 µM adapter and 3 µL nuclease‑free water (total 37.3 µL). Mix thoroughly, brief spin, and incubate at 20 °C for 2 h (optional up to 4 h at 20 °C or 12 h at 4 °C). Store the ligation at 23 °C for ≤24 h, at 4 °C for ≤3 days, or at –20 °C for ≤4 weeks.

steps.title: Biotin pull‑down of ligated DNA
steps.instruction: Prepare 1× binding/washing buffer and 2× binding buffer. Vortex 5 µL streptavidin C1 beads, resuspend in 100 µL 1× buffer, vortex ≥30 s or rotate 5 min. Magnet‑separate 1 min, discard supernatant; repeat wash three times. Resuspend beads in 37 µL 2× binding buffer. Mix equal volume of the 37 µL adapter‑ligated DNA with the bead suspension (final DNA concentration 5 µg/µL; NaCl reduced from 2 M to 1 M). Incubate 20 min at 23 °C in a vertical mixer. Magnet‑separate 2 min, discard supernatant. Wash beads three times with 200 µL 1× washing buffer (magnet 2–3 min each). Finally resuspend beads in 10 µL Elution buffer.

steps.title: PCR amplification of Hi‑C library
steps.instruction: Prepare a 50 µL PCR master mix: 10 µL adapter‑ligated library, 5 µL 10× KAPA Library Amplification Primer Mix, 25 µL 2× KAPA HiFi HotStart Ready‑Mix, and 10 µL nuclease‑free water. Run thermocycler: 98 °C 45 s; 98 °C 15 s; 12–16 cycles of 60 °C 30 s and 72 °C 30 s; final extension 72 °C 1 min; hold 4 °C.

steps.title: AMPure XP bead purification (optional)
steps.instruction: Bring AMPure XP beads to 20 °C. Add 60 µL (1.2× volume) beads to each 50 µL PCR product. Mix, incubate 10 min at 23 °C, mixing intermittently. Magnet 2 min, discard supernatant. While on magnet, add 200 µL fresh 80 % ethanol, incubate 30 s at 23 °C, remove ethanol. Repeat ethanol wash once more, then air‑dry beads 3–5 min at 23 °C (avoid over‑drying). Resuspend beads in 21 µL Elution buffer, pipette 10×. Incubate 2 min at 23 °C, magnet 1 min, transfer 20 µL clear eluate to a new tube. Store at 20 °C up to 1 week.

steps.title: Size selection on 2% E‑Gel
steps.instruction: Load 20 µL of purified library into adjacent lanes of a 2 % E‑Gel EX agarose gel containing SYBR Gold. Load 6 µL 50 bp ladder as size marker. Run the gel on an electrophoresis device. Excise the gel region corresponding to 250–600 bp fragments and place the gel slice into a low‑binding 1.5 mL tube.

steps.title: Gel extraction and column purification
steps.instruction: Weigh the gel slice, add 1 volume XP2 Binding Buffer, and incubate 7 min at 50–60 °C (vortex/shake every 2–3 min) until fully melted. Connect a HiBind DNA Mini Column to a vacuum manifold. Transfer ≤700 µL of melt to the column, centrifuge 23 °C, 13,500 g, 1 min; discard flow‑through. Repeat transfers until all melt is processed. Add 300 µL XP2 Binding Buffer, centrifuge 1 min, discard flow‑through. Add 700 µL SPW Buffer (pre‑diluted with 100 % ethanol), centrifuge 1 min, discard; repeat SPW wash once more. Spin the empty column 2 min at max speed to dry the matrix. Transfer the column to a clean 1.5 mL tube, add 20 µL Elution Buffer (or deionized water) to the membrane center, sit 2 min at 23 °C, centrifuge 1 min at max speed. Store purified DNA at –20 °C.

steps.title: Quantify library with Qubit
steps.instruction: Measure DNA concentration of the final sis‑Hi‑C library using a Qubit dsDNA Broad Range kit according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

description: The in situ Hi-C (Hi-C) procedure involves several key steps, including formaldehyde cross-linking (fixation), enzyme digestion, end-repair with biotin labeling, ligation, decrosslinking, DNA extraction, and high-throughput sequencing.2,3 The process requires frequent centrifugation, washing, and tube changes, as well as precise DNA fragment size selection, which can impact DNA yield and quantity. As a result, traditional Hi-C methods typically require millions of cells, which limits their applicability in research on embryonic development, tumors, and clinical diseases. Recent developments in small-scale in situ Hi-C (sis-Hi-C) have successfully reduced the required cell input to as few as 100 cells by scaling down the reaction system and minimizing experimental steps and tube rotations, thus preventing sample and DNA loss.4,5,6 Building on these improvements, we have further optimized the sis-Hi-C method, enabling the generation of high-quality Hi-C data from as few as 50–100 bovine embryonic cells. Using Alu I digestion instead of sonication is a key feature of our protocol. It enables more controlled fragmentation and reduces material loss, which is especially important for low-input samples. Furthermore, transferring embryonic cells via glass capillaries and fixing them with formaldehyde in droplets on disposable plastic culture dishes significantly reduces cell loss compared to conventional fixation in centrifuge tubes, which is especially beneficial for low-input samples. This protocol enables the study of chromatin interactions within the 3D nuclear space. More importantly, it applies to oocytes and all stages of pre-implantation embryos in cattle, and it holds potential for application in human and porcine embryos as well. The following protocol details the specific steps for using 8-cell bovine embryos, though it has been successfully used for germinal-vesicle (GV) oocytes, 4-cell embryos and blastocysts.
